method: Exact saint/episode identity checked against institutional records where available; inventory conflicts and image rights held separately, no physical pixel/image QA

summary.methodological_caveat: Institutional source may establish work identity while exact uploaded digital asset and image reuse remain unchecked

rules: No replacement of historical owner choices or accepted alternatives
No source-catalogue endorsement of the precise photographic file unless checked
Museum/current-collection identity and lost artwork survival status are separate claims
Depicted saint or tradition is not necessarily the appointed Gospel

records.artwork_title: The Temptation of Saint Anthony the Great
records.physical_work_identity: KMSKA Antwerp 103, Maerten de Vos, 1594, oil on panel
records.findings: KMSKA identifies the desert father Anthony the Great, his temptation and associated demons. This is a saint-life subject matching the feast, not a depicted Mass Gospel.

records.physical_work_identity: Musée des Beaux-Arts de Dijon, martyrdom of Sebastian; Jacopo Bassano per museum educational PDF, historical 19th-century catalogue labels Leandro Bassano
records.findings: Dijon identifies a Martyrdom of St Sebastian by Jacopo Bassano. An older catalogue labels a St Sebastian martyrdom under Leandro Bassano; verify artwork inventory/object before treating the historical label as an alternative attribution for this exact painting.

records.artwork_title: Two Girls as Saint Agnes and Saint Dorothea
records.physical_work_identity: KMSKA Antwerp 599, Michaelina Wautier, historiated double portrait
records.findings: Museum explicitly says two unidentified real girls pose as Agnes (lamb) and Dorothea (flowers/fruit). Keep feast iconographic relation, but not a biographical or martyrdom scene.

records.artwork_title: Sainte Martine refusant d'adorer les idoles 02
records.physical_work_identity: Musée Granet Aix-en-Provence, state INV 107 / MR 413, Pietro da Cortona, oil on copper, 49.8×34.8cm
records.findings: The exact Commons title and photo describe the Granet oil-on-copper object. Do not conflate with Princeton 1998-38 oil-on-canvas, the Pitti version, or copies catalogued by Zeri. Granet photo licensing/Italy-France use context is separate.

records.artwork_title: The Citizens of Antwerp Return Sacred Vessels to Saint Norbert
records.findings: Institutional iconography explicitly names St Norbert, Antwerp citizens, returned monstrance and sacred vessels hidden from Tankelin. Good saint-life association, not a Gospel illustration.

records.artwork_title: Saint Anthony of Padua with the Christ Child
records.physical_work_identity: Staatliche Museen zu Berlin Gemäldegalerie inventory 414 (obj:862397), Murillo 1670–1680, recorded likely destroyed May 1945
records.findings: The Berlin museum says this particular inventory 414 was probably destroyed in the Friedrichshain flak bunker in May 1945. A Commons image sourced from the catalogue is not proof of a surviving object or current museum holding. Other versions and copies exist; do not silently substitute one.

records.physical_work_identity: Musea Brugge Groeningemuseum 0000.GRO0204.I, Hugo van der Goes, c.1475–1482
records.findings: Institution describes the death/dormition of the Virgin with apostles and Christ above. Appropriate anticipation of the Assumption vigil; not the appointed Gospel episode or a literal painting of bodily assumption.

records.artwork_title: The Virgin and Child Appearing to Saint Hyacinth
records.physical_work_identity: Louvre INV 186 / MR 140, Ludovico Carracci 1594, oil on canvas 3.75×2.23m
records.findings: The Louvre authenticates the painting and a related preparatory drawing. Vision is hagiographic (according to Louvre commentary associated with Assumption Day 1224), not a Mass Gospel episode. Do not confuse painting INV186 with drawing RFML.AG.2019.47.1.

records.physical_work_identity: Versailles accession MV 7669; on deposit at Musée Fabre Montpellier (Versailles institution press record)
records.findings: The painting honors Louis IX, not an episode in the Mass Gospel. A Versailles press record distinguishes Versailles ownership/deposit at Montpellier; Commons collection names may conceal this distinction.

Institution confirms the mystic St Teresa of Ávila in ecstasy/transverberation with angel and pierced-heart iconography. The proposed Commons jpeg is only 706×939, so verify superior institutional CC0 reproduction and mobile legibility.

records.observance: Presentation of the Blessed Virgin Mary
records.artwork_title: Presentation of the Virgin in the Temple
records.physical_work_identity: Musée Granet Aix-en-Provence 860.1.408, Lubin Baugin 1647; note separate Rennes preparatory sketch
records.findings: The depicted event is the traditional Presentation of Mary, not a narrated canonical Gospel pericope. Distinguish Granet painting from the smaller Rennes sketch; original Claude Commons file is only 1024×814 and is not itself a photo release gate.

records.physical_work_identity: Strasbourg Musée des Beaux-Arts 453.b, Bernardino Fungai c.1500, predella panel
records.findings: INHA RETIF identifies Saint Clement reunited with his family as a panel of the St Clement cycle. A related INHA 'Conversion of Saint Clement' entry misstates the reunification panel as 453.a; independent related-results table says 453.b. Hold cross-reference consistency rather than mixing two predella paintings.
